fields.description: Hours an unpaid InstaPay/Mobile Wallet order can sit Out for Delivery awaiting payment before the hourly escalation job alerts managers.

fields.description: Base64url-encoded uncompressed EC public key served to browsers for pushManager.subscribe(). Auto-generated on first use.
fields.label: VAPID Public Key

fields.description: PEM-format EC private key used to sign VAPID push requests. Auto-generated on first use. Never expose this value.
fields.label: VAPID Private Key

fields.description: URL or mailto: identifying the push sender to Apple/Google push servers.
fields.label: VAPID Subject

fields.description: Master switch for the post-dispatch return workflow. When off, the return endpoints refuse and the client hides the action. Turning it off is the instant rollback lever — it needs no deploy or restart.
fields.label: Enable Invoice Returns

fields.description: Master switch for the per-invoice courier transitions (Arrived / Delivered / Failed). When off, the service refuses and the courier app hides the actions. Read in the service, not the API, so every caller — HTTP, harness, background job — hits the same gate. Instant rollback lever: no deploy, no restart.
fields.label: Enable Courier Delivery Actions

fields.description: Refuse the Out for Delivery move when the order's delivery address carries no location pin. Off by default so the door-pin database can fill up first — turning it on is what makes staff paste a maps link, and turning it off again is the instant rollback lever (no deploy, no restart). Enforced in jarz_pos.services.ofd_pin_gate, which BOTH the Kanban single-invoice path and the Delivery Trip bulk path call.
fields.label: Require Delivery Pin Before Out for Delivery

fields.description: Master switch for the customer-facing /track/TOKEN page and its guest JSON endpoint. Off by default: this is the only guest-callable surface in the app, so it must be switchable off in seconds without a deploy. Read in jarz_pos.services.tracking, not in the API layer, so every entry point hits the same gate.
fields.label: Enable Customer Delivery Tracking

fields.description: Show the courier's phone number on the customer tracking page. Off by default: a tracking link can be forwarded to anyone, so publishing a staff mobile number is a decision, not a default.
fields.label: Show Courier Phone To Customer

fields.description: Release the courier's live position and name to every customer whose order is Out for Delivery, instead of only the one the courier is currently driving toward. OFF is the safe value and is what an unset field reads as. Turn it on ONLY on a site whose courier app cannot yet mark a trip leg: dispatch sends a whole trip Out for Delivery at once, so with this on, every customer in a slot watches the courier visit the other addresses first, in order, with the courier's name beside the marker.
fields.label: Allow Live Map Without A Trip Leg

fields.description: How many hours a tracking link keeps working after the order reaches a terminal state (Delivered / Cancelled / Returned). After that the token resolves to the same generic "not found" as a wrong token — never a distinguishable "expired", which would confirm that the token was once real. 0 means never expire.
fields.label: Tracking Link TTL (hours)

fields.description: How many days back a manager may post a production batch. Beyond this only a System Manager may go, because that is the range that reaches a closed accounting period. Operators can never backdate at all.
fields.label: Production Max Backdate Days

fields.description: Largest material value (at valuation rate) one operator may commit in a single batch. 0 means no limit. Managers always bypass it.
fields.label: Operator Batch Value Limit

fields.description: Allow finishing a batch with more good output than the Work Order planned. Off by default: a quantity above plan is far more often a typo than a genuine over-yield.
fields.label: Allow Over-Production

fields.description: Sub-assembly whose default BOM defines one batch for the Daily Production Plan. Deliberately Data and not Link: a stale Link on this Single blocks every full save of it, and a mistyped name here degrades to the built-in default rather than locking the Settings form. Leave blank to use 'Cheesecake Mix'.
fields.label: Production Mix Item

fields.description: Batch sizes the mixer accepts in one run and how well each mixes, e.g. '1:poor, 1.5:preferred, 2:acceptable'. Quality is what the plan optimises: a preferred run is free, acceptable costs a little, poor costs a lot, and a wasted batch of mix outweighs any of them. Leave blank for the default above. A bare size with no quality keeps its known ranking.
fields.label: Mixer Run Sizes

fields.description: Where purchased stock lands when nothing more specific applies. Resolution order per line: warehouse chosen on the line → the Item's own default warehouse for the company → the Item Group routes below → this warehouse. Set this to the raw-materials store, since that is what most purchases are.
fields.label: Default Purchase Warehouse

fields.description: Route purchases to a warehouse by Item Group — e.g. Raw Material → the raw-materials store, Consumable → the consumables store. The most specific matching group wins, so a child group overrides its parent.
fields.label: Purchase Warehouse Routes

fields.description: Purchase Taxes and Charges Template applied to new purchases by default (e.g. the 14% VAT template). Leave blank for no default; the buyer can always change it.
fields.label: Default Purchase Taxes Template

fields.description: Item Tax Template a purchase line falls back to when the Item master declares no tax of its own — the site's standard purchase VAT (14%). Precedence per line: the template chosen on the line (choosing none means untaxed) → the Item's own Item Tax row → this default. Leave blank for no default.
fields.label: Default Purchase VAT Template

fields.description: Require the supplier's own invoice/bill number on every purchase. ERPNext already rejects a duplicate bill number for the same supplier, so turning this on makes that guard actually bite.
fields.label: Require Supplier Bill Number

fields.description: Default lead time in days for a team item request — used as the 'needed by' date when the requester does not pick one.
fields.label: Request Default Lead Days

fields.description: Fastest the print house turns a label batch around, in working days.
fields.label: Print Lead Days (Min)

fields.description: Slowest the print house turns a label batch around, in working days. Reorder alerts are timed against this one.
fields.label: Print Lead Days (Max)

fields.description: Weekly day the print house is closed. It is skipped when counting printing days, so a 3-day batch ordered Wednesday is ready Sunday, not Saturday.
fields.label: Printing Rest Day
fields.options:
None
Friday
Saturday
Sunday
Friday & Saturday

fields.description: Extra days of cover on top of the print lead time before a label is flagged Reorder Soon.
fields.label: Reorder Buffer Days

fields.description: Labels on one printed sheet for Medium jars.
fields.label: Labels Per Sheet (Medium)

fields.description: Labels on one printed sheet for Large jars.
fields.label: Labels Per Sheet (Large)

fields.description: Sheets ordered per flavor when nothing else is set on the label.
fields.label: Default Print Batch (Sheets)

fields.description: Draw labels down automatically when a Sales Invoice is submitted for a customer that has a tracked label. Leave on: with it off the ledger only moves when somebody records a count by hand.
fields.label: Auto-Consume Labels On Invoice

fields.description: Send the daily 'labels running low' alert to managers and B2B reps.
fields.label: Enable Label Reorder Alerts

fields.description: Asset account debited by label print Purchase Invoices. Its balance should always equal the value of labels on the shelves.
fields.label: Labels Inventory Account

fields.description: COGS account label cost moves into as labels are consumed by invoices.
fields.label: Label Cost (COGS) Account

fields.description: The non-stock item label print batches are billed against on the supplier's Purchase Invoice.
fields.label: Label Printing Item

fields.description: Post the Journal Entry that moves label cost from inventory to COGS as labels are consumed. Turn off only if labels should stay a pure count with no GL impact.
fields.label: Post Label COGS Journal Entries
Route Engine
fields.description: auto = use the OSRM server when it is configured and answering, else straight-line estimates. straight_line pins it to estimates (the kill switch: no deploy, no restart). osrm behaves as auto - OSRM is never trusted blindly, because a route that fails to plan is worse than one that is approximate.

fields.label: OSRM Base URL
fields.description: Root of a self-hosted OSRM server, e.g. http://10.0.0.5:5000. Empty means every distance is a straight-line estimate. Never point this at a public demo server for production traffic.

fields.label: OSRM Timeout (seconds)
fields.description: Clamped to 1-15. A routing call sits inside a user-facing request; a slow one gets abandoned in favour of the estimate.

fields.label: Road Detour Factor
fields.description: Multiplier turning straight-line kilometres into driving kilometres when OSRM is not in play. 1.35 suits dense Cairo. Ignored entirely when OSRM answers.

fields.label: Average Speed (km/h)
fields.description: Door-to-door average including traffic and parking. Keep it pessimistic: a day plan that cannot be driven gets abandoned by lunchtime.

fields.label: Default Visit Minutes
fields.description: Time inside a venue, when the stop does not say otherwise.

fields.label: Default Max Stops Per Day
fields.description: What the auto-planner aims for. A rep can still add more by hand, up to the hard ceiling of 60.

fields.label: Working Day (minutes)
fields.description: Total budget for driving plus visits. The auto-planner drops its lowest-priority stops until the day fits.

fields.label: Default Start Time
fields.description: When a new route is assumed to leave, used to estimate arrival times.

fields.label: Field Visit Days
fields.description: Comma-separated weekday names the team does field visits on, e.g. Saturday,Sunday. Empty means any day. Advisory only - it steers the planner's suggestions and never blocks a date.

fields.label: Stale After (days)
fields.description: A door not visited in this long is flagged as due. Feeds the auto-planner's priority and the leads filter.
